newsitem.title: UK: 16 charged after London clashes with police.
newsitem.headline: 16 charged after London clashes with police.

text.p: Sixteen people were charged with various offences on Sunday after violence erupted during a rally in London in support of sacked dock workers.
The charges included actual bodily harm, criminal damage and violent disorder, police said. About 1,000 police in riot gear were called in to quell the disturbances on Saturday.

At least four policemen were injured when about 100 protesters, wearing masks and hoods, bombarded them with cans, paint, sticks and smoke bombs at the entrance to Prime Minister John Major's official residence in Downing Street.

The protesters were forced back to Trafalgar Square, north of Downing Street, where the main bulk of the 7,000 marchers arrived peacefully for a rally in support of dockers from the northern port of Liverpool.
A police spokeswoman said protesters broke up paving stones and used the pieces as missiles. One man emerged from the melee with blood pouring from his face.
